strengths: Clear conceptual motivation: The paper clearly identifies and formalizes the core drawback of standard masked discrete diffusion (irreversibility) and unguided re-masking techniques (sample inefficiency and stochasticity).

Principled framework with theoretical connection: Formulating masked diffusion through the star-shaped paradigm simplifies the reverse posterior and reveals an insightful mathematical connection to ReMDM while avoiding ReMDM's brittle hyperparameter tuning.

Comprehensive empirical analysis: The ablation studies (analyzing the phase-dependent nature of generation, optimal activation time, loop size, error predictor temperature, and parameter efficiency) are thorough and provide convincing insight into the dynamics of discrete diffusion refinement.

Scalability and practical relevance: The method is successfully applied across diverse settings, ranging from unconditional text generation on OpenWebText to conditional code generation on Conala and scaling up to a 7B instruction-tuned model (Dream-Instruct 7B), showing consistent improvements across seven standard benchmarks.
weaknesses: Lack of wall-clock inference runtime comparisons: While the error predictor can be as small as a single transformer block or a linear head on frozen representations, running the error predictor at every refinement step introduces computational overhead. Reporting actual wall-clock inference time and latency comparisons against MDLM and ReMDM would provide a more complete assessment of practical efficiency.

Auxiliary training overhead: Unlike purely training-free sampling methods (such as ReMDM), G-Star requires simulating corrupted states and training an auxiliary error predictor model, adding complexity to the deployment pipeline.

Discrepancy in Dream-Instruct baseline reproduction: On certain benchmarks in Table 3 (e.g., IFEval drops from 62.5 in the original paper to 56.4 reproduced, GPQA drops from 33.0 to 31.0), the reproduced baseline is noticeably lower than the published numbers. Although +G-Star improves upon the reproduced baseline, clarifying the source of these discrepancies would strengthen the evaluation.

strengths: Principled and intuitive formulation: The paper effectively addresses a fundamental limitation of masked diffusion language models—the irreversibility of token commitments—by adapting the star-shaped diffusion framework to discrete text, making the connection to ReMDM explicit and eliminating tedious hyperparameter tuning for re-masking rates.

Targeted error revision: The introduction of a learned error predictor (g_phi) to guide remasking is well-motivated and solves the sample inefficiency of random/indiscriminate remasking in previous approaches.

Parameter-efficient design: The error predictor can be trained simply as a lightweight linear classification head on top of frozen representations of the base diffusion model, achieving performance on par with full model fine-tuning with minimal parameter footprint.

Comprehensive empirical validation: The method is validated thoroughly across unconditional language modeling (OWT), code generation (Conala), and large-scale instruction-tuned models (Dream-Instruct 7B across 7 downstream benchmarks including MMLU, GSM8K, and IFEval), showing consistent improvements.

Insightful ablations and analysis: The paper provides clear insights into the two-phase dynamics of generation (drafting vs. late-stage refinement), activation timing (t_on), loop sizes, and the temperature-controlled quality-diversity trade-off.
weaknesses: Unreported inference latency / wall-clock overhead: In the guided sampling step (Algorithm 2), evaluating the error predictor on the discrete candidate sequence x_hat_0 (logits_err = g_phi(x_hat_0)) requires an extra forward pass through the transformer backbone during each refinement step. The paper discusses parameter overhead but lacks concrete wall-clock latency comparisons against baselines with equal compute time.

Metric limitations in code evaluation: The Conala benchmark is evaluated purely via conditional perplexity under Qwen2.5-Coder rather than functional correctness / execution accuracy (such as pass@k on HumanEval/MBPP for the Conala model, although HumanEval/MBPP are evaluated for Dream-Instruct 7B).

Modest gains on certain downstream tasks: For Dream-Instruct 7B (Table 3), while tasks like IFEval (+2.9) and GPQA (+1.8) see noticeable gains, tasks like GSM8K exhibit only marginal improvement (+0.1, 81.5 vs. 81.6), and some reproduced baseline numbers noticeably deviate from the originally published results (e.g., IFEval reproduced at 56.4 vs. 62.5 published).

strengths: Principled reformulation: Adapting the star-shaped diffusion framework to discrete masked language modeling provides an elegant theoretical justification for bidirectional token editing and connects naturally to remasking heuristics.

Insightful analysis of sampling dynamics: The identification and empirical verification of the 'two-phase' nature of masked diffusion (early-stage drafting requiring monotonic unmasking vs. late-stage refinement benefiting from error revision) is well-motivated and convincingly explained via step-to-step similarity and activation time ablations.

Parameter-efficient design: Demonstrating that a lightweight classification head on top of a frozen backbone performs comparably to full fine-tuning of the error predictor makes the proposed guidance mechanism practically accessible without requiring full model retraining.

Comprehensive empirical scope: The method is validated across unconditional text generation (OWT), conditional code generation (Conala), and scaled up to an instruction-tuned 7B model (Dream-Instruct) across seven diverse reasoning and generation benchmarks.
weaknesses: Mathematical inconsistency in Algorithm 1: Line 12 specifies `p <- Softmax(g_phi(\hat{x}_0))`, whereas Line 13 defines the loss as a token-wise binary cross-entropy (`y_i log p_i + (1 - y_i) log(1 - p_i)`). Binary cross-entropy requires independent Bernoulli probabilities per token via `Sigmoid`, whereas `Softmax` normalizes across the sequence length, rendering the stated objective mathematically mismatched.

Omission of inference runtime and wall-clock latency: While the error predictor is parameter-efficient, evaluating it at each refinement step requires an additional forward pass through the transformer backbone (for the 12B-H and 7B configurations). The paper claims low overhead but does not report wall-clock generation times or throughput comparisons against MDLM and ReMDM.

Quality-diversity trade-off and potential mode collapse: The guided sampler achieves extremely low perplexity (e.g., 9.9 at 512 steps in Table 1) at the expense of a substantial drop in n-gram diversity (DIV drops from 37.8 to 26.4), which also causes MAUVE to peak early and degrade at 512 steps. Further analysis is needed to verify whether the model is falling into repetitive or overly conservative generation modes.

Missing ablation on self-confidence guided star sampling: The paper compares G-Star against unguided Star-loop and ReMDM variants, but does not evaluate a Star-loop baseline guided directly by the base model's internal token probabilities or prediction entropy, leaving it unclear how much gain comes specifically from the auxiliary trained head versus simple confidence-based rank targeting.

Lack of statistical significance reporting: Downstream benchmark results on Dream-Instruct 7B (Table 3) show narrow margins on several tasks (e.g., +0.1 on GSM8K, +1.2 on HumanEval, +1.4 on MBPP). Given the stochastic nature of discrete diffusion sampling, error bars or standard deviations across multiple random seeds are needed to verify statistical significance.
Citation formatting issues: Several in-text citations appear incomplete (e.g., referencing 'Wang et al.' without publication year on pages 1, 2, 3, 7, and 12).

strengths: Clean theoretical grounding: The paper establishes a clear mathematical connection between the star-shaped discrete diffusion formulation and prior remasking frameworks (e.g., ReMDM with \sigma_t = 1 - \alpha_{t-1}), and provides an exact derivation of the VLB simplifying to a weighted cross-entropy loss that justifies reusing pre-trained MDLM weights.

Principled error detection design: Training the error predictor g_phi directly on the diffusion model's own sampled candidate errors avoids the artificial distribution shift common in prior work (such as uniform token corruption) while remaining lightweight and plug-and-play as a head on frozen representations.

Thorough empirical analysis and insights: The analysis of sampling dynamics (Section 4.2 and Figures 1-2) provides insightful justification for why star-shaped sampling fails when applied uniformly across early steps (due to context sparsity and step-to-step instability) and why late-stage/loop activation is optimal.

Comprehensive evaluation across scales: Experiments cover unconditional text generation on OpenWebText (including Pareto frontiers across denoiser temperatures), code generation on Conala, and scale up to Dream-Instruct 7B across multiple standard downstream reasoning and coding benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA, IFEval, HumanEval).
weaknesses: Inference latency overhead: As shown in Table 4, evaluating the error predictor on the clean estimate x_0 adds between 20% to 50% additional forward pass overhead per guided step. While Pareto comparisons show that G-Star at 128 steps outperforms ReMDM at 512 steps, an explicit Pareto curve parameterized directly by wall-clock latency (rather than solely step count) across all methods would make the efficiency comparison even more direct.

Modest performance delta on large-scale reasoning tasks: The improvements on Dream-Instruct 7B (Table 1) are modest on some tasks (e.g., GSM8K moving from 81.5 to 81.6, HumanEval from 53.7 to 54.9), although gains on IFEval (+2.9) and GPQA (+1.8) remain respectable.

Inherent limitation to in-place edits: As the authors honestly note in the limitations, the formulation is strictly restricted to substitution and cannot easily accommodate length variations, token insertions, or deletions.

strengths: Principled theoretical framing: The paper establishes a clear mathematical connection between the star-shaped diffusion formulation and existing remasking frameworks (specifically ReMDM), demonstrating that star-shaped masked diffusion naturally corresponds to maximal remasking flexibility that can be stabilized with guidance.

Targeted error detection on realistic error distributions: Rather than training a refiner on synthetic uniform random replacements or relying on uncalibrated model confidences, the error predictor is trained explicitly to identify the nuanced, contextually plausible errors produced by the diffusion model itself.

Parameter- and compute-efficient design: The error detector can be implemented as a lightweight head atop the frozen diffusion backbone (12B, H), requiring no retraining of the base model and introducing negligible parameter and memory overhead.

Thorough empirical analysis and Pareto evaluations: The paper comprehensively characterizes the two-phase dynamics (drafting vs. refinement), provides rigorous Pareto frontier comparisons over denoiser temperatures, and validates robustness across out-of-domain corpora (e.g., code, math, news).
Effective scaling to large models: G-Star demonstrates consistent gains when applied to the state-of-the-art Dream-Instruct 7B model across seven diverse benchmarks, including MMLU, GPQA, and IFEval.
weaknesses: Additional latency per step: Because evaluating the error predictor requires an additional pass through the backbone during the refinement phase, G-Star incurs an increased latency per step (up to ~50% overhead depending on the fraction of guided steps), although this is partially offset by achieving superior quality at significantly lower total step budgets.

Code evaluation limited to perplexity: For the Conala code generation experiment (Section 5.2), evaluation is reported only via conditional perplexity under Qwen2.5B-Coder rather than functional execution metrics (such as pass@k or execution correctness), which would provide a stronger test of code generation fidelity.

Evaluation on Dream-Instruct 7B is conducted only in high-step regimes: In Section 5.1, the evaluation follows the baseline's full-sequence step budget (T = seq_len, up to 1280 steps). It remains unverified whether the strong few-step acceleration observed on OpenWebText translates directly to the 7B instruction-tuned setting.

strengths: Clear motivation addressing a fundamental bottleneck in masked diffusion language models (MDLMs): the irreversibility of token unmasking and the resulting inability to perform iterative error correction.

Insightful analysis of sampling dynamics (Sections 4.2 and 4.3): the paper clearly explains and demonstrates why pure star-shaped diffusion diverges in early stages due to sparse context, and demonstrates that a two-phase hybrid schedule (MDLM drafting followed by late-stage star-shaped refinement) resolves the stability-flexibility trade-off.

Targeted error detection on actual model mistakes rather than synthetic uniform noise: Algorithm 1 effectively trains the predictor $g_\phi$ to detect the specific error distribution produced by the base diffusion model, leading to structured, contiguous phrase-level corrections (as evidenced in Figures 9 and 13).

Rigorous theoretical grounding: Proposition 1 formalizes the mathematical connection between the star-shaped sampler and ReMDM (showing equivalence when $\sigma_t = 1 - \alpha_{t-1}$), and Claim 1 establishes the VLB relationship to the standard MDLM training objective.

Extensive empirical evaluation and scaling: results span unconditional generation on OpenWebText, conditional code generation on Conala, and successful integration with a large-scale 7B parameter diffusion model (Dream-Instruct 7B) across seven standard benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, GPQA, IFEval).

Thorough ablations and computational transparency: includes full Pareto frontier comparisons over denoiser temperatures, predictor capacity comparisons (1B vs. 12B, head-only vs. full), out-of-domain robustness checks (Table 3), and wall-clock latency/NFE measurements (Table 4).
weaknesses: Incremental conceptual distance from ReMDM: As shown in Proposition 1, the unguided star-shaped sampler is mathematically equivalent to ReMDM under a specific parameter setting ($σ_t = 1 - \alpha_{t-1}$), meaning the primary conceptual innovation lies in the hybrid scheduling heuristic and the addition of the learned error prediction guidance module rather than an entirely new generative paradigm.

Evaluation metrics on code generation: Table 2 evaluates code generation on Conala solely using conditional perplexity from an external model (Qwen2.5-Coder), rather than execution-based accuracy metrics (e.g., Pass@k) or surface-matching metrics (e.g., BLEU / CodeBLEU).

Modest gains on certain downstream 7B benchmarks: In Table 1, while gains on IFEval (+2.9) and GPQA (+1.8) are meaningful, improvements on math and code benchmarks like GSM8K (81.5 to 81.6) and MBPP (58.0 to 59.4) are marginal and within typical sampling variance.

Inference latency overhead: The targeted error predictor incurs additional Transformer forward passes during the refinement phase (e.g., increasing step latency by 20% to 50% for 12B variants, as detailed in Table 4), although this is partially compensated for by requiring fewer total diffusion steps along the Pareto frontier.
